title: The Lifecycle of "Facts": A Survey of Social Bias in Knowledge Graphs

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated through descriptive statistics of entity representation, Named Entity Recognition (NER) and Relation Extraction (RE) error rates using counterfactual names, semantic polarity classifiers, stereotypical analogy testing via cosine similarity, projection onto a bias subspace, update-based translational likelihood metrics, and demographic/predictive parity in downstream link prediction tasks.

Measured via descriptive statistics of ethnic group mentions in knowledge graphs, analysis of ontological gaps in medical contexts, and evaluating NER system accuracy degradation on synthetic sentences containing non-white names compared to white names.

Assessed by applying sentiment and regard classifiers to measure the semantic polarity of natural language statements generated from knowledge graph triples involving different religious entities (e.g., Islam, Christianity, Hinduism).

Evaluated using descriptive statistics to map the coverage of location entries in knowledge graphs against real-world global population densities, highlighting the underrepresentation of non-Western regions.

Analyzed by measuring the semantic polarity and sentiment associated with different professions (e.g., CEO vs. prisoner), and by computing embedding projection scores and link prediction correlations against demographic seed dimensions.
